questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real, everyday DBA task this course has been building toward?
options: Opening a script someone else already wrote, understanding it well enough to trust it, and changing one thing safely
Writing large, original PowerShell modules from a blank file on a regular basis
Memorizing every cmdlet in the Az and dbatools modules by name
Avoiding PowerShell scripts entirely in favor of clicking through SSMS and the Azure Portal
questions.explain: This matches the course's stated goal from Lesson 1: read, modify, and run — not write from scratch.

questions.q: What real gap does reading Test-BackupAge closely surface?
options: Invoke-DbaQuery throws an error if a server is unreachable, and with no error handling that crashes the entire script, skipping every server after it
The script has no function at all and only contains loose commands
The script accidentally deletes databases instead of checking their backup status
The script cannot connect to any SQL Server instance under any circumstance
questions.explain: Without a try/catch, one unreachable server stops the whole script instead of just that one server's check.

questions.q: What does the try/catch modification actually do?
options: It catches a connection failure for one server, reports it clearly, and lets the outer foreach loop continue checking the remaining servers
It permanently disables backup checking for any server that fails once
It silently ignores all errors with no message at all
It rewrites the T-SQL query to avoid ever needing a live connection
questions.explain: try runs the risky call, catch handles a failure without crashing, and return exits only that one function call.

questions.q: Why is adding the $LogPath parameter considered a safe modification?
options: It's additive and backward-compatible — it's a new, defaulted parameter, so existing calls that don't pass it keep working unchanged
It completely rewrites how the function's parameters work, breaking all previous calls
It removes the need for the function to accept a -SqlInstance parameter
It changes the query so it no longer checks backup history at all
questions.explain: A defaulted parameter (Lesson 13's pattern) means nothing about existing calls has to change for the script to keep working.

questions.q: What does this lesson's career-path verification confirm, and what should a learner do at this lesson's end?
options: It confirms all 7 courses across both the Job Ready and Advanced stages of the Azure Database Administrator path are complete, and there's no Lesson 19 to move to next
It confirms only the Job Ready stage is complete, with PowerShell Fundamentals still ahead
It confirms this course is unrelated to any career path in the catalog
It confirms a ninth course still needs to be built before the path is done
questions.explain: T-SQL Development, Azure Fundamentals, Azure Database Administrator, Data Factory, Terraform & Bicep, and Git/GitHub/CI-CD were all verified fully built, so this course's completion closes the entire path.
